A **channel** is a place where a merchant's store sells products. Storefront websites, marketplaces like Amazon and eBay, point-of-sale systems, and marketing feeds are all sales channels. A custom channel may not fit into any one of these types.

identifier: A channel is defined by the following
statement: A channel is defined by the following: * A `name`, which is merchant-defined for internal convenience and not exposed to shoppers * A `type`, which may be one of the following: * `storefront`, * `marketing`, * `pos`, * `marketplace` * `custom` * A `platform`, which indicates the platform on which shoppers primarily use the channel

Each BigCommerce store is provisioned with one channel out of the box, intended for its first Stencil storefront. The ID of this channel is `1` for all BigCommerce stores. This channel may also be referred to as the "default channel", and it cannot be deleted.

A **site** is a website owned or controlled exclusively by the merchant, usually for hosting a storefront website. Every site will be tied to exactly one channel, but because not all sales channels are sites, channels are not required to have a site. Sites are mainly relevant to storefront-type channels, and they serve as containers for settings and objects that only apply to websites.
The first Stencil storefront of each merchant store has an ID of `1000` and is also known as the default site. It cannot be deleted.
Allowed values for a channel's `status` vary by channel `type`.
`storefront` | `prelaunch`, `active`, `inactive`, `archived`, `deleted`
`marketing`, `marketplace`, `pos` | `connected`, `disconnected`, `archived`, `deleted`

You can restore a Channel with `deleted` status within **90 days** after deletion by contacting the BigCommerce support team. After the 90-days grace period is over, the Channel `status` will become `terminated`.
The `terminated` status is read-only. Channels with a `status` of `terminated` **cannot** be restored.

Multi-Storefront (MSF) allows you to use a single BigCommerce “store” to power multiple “storefronts”. Each of these storefronts can have its own unique domain, theme, categories, web pages, social media links, price lists, email templates, and more. The settings and data for each of these storefronts are managed from one BigCommerce control panel.

Depending on your business model, multi-storefront may work for some merchants as a multi-region or cross-border solution. However, some store functions are global and are shared across storefronts, such as the built-in blog. Additionally, even though the same product can be assigned to different storefronts, product attributes (like description and name) cannot be overridden into a different language without customization. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields.
Multi-storefront can be useful for merchants who have multiple brands or who serve multiple segments like B2C, B2B, retail, and wholesale segments.

With multiple native storefronts, you can do all of this within the control panel: Create and manage multiple BigCommerce storefronts within a single control panel. Configure storefront settings and internal notifications for each storefront. Connect different domain names and SSL certificates for each storefront. Apply and customize themes, page templates, email templates, widgets, web pages, scripts, and social media links for each storefront. Set and manage default storefront currency and unique sets of currencies per storefront. Configure unique checkout settings per storefront. Set up web analytics (like Google Analytics) specific to each storefront. Set up a Meta Pixel specific to each storefront. Create storefront-unique categories and make products available on one or multiple storefronts. Stores on a Performance plan will have access to additional product localization fields. Configure inventory settings for each storefront, including notifications. Control product filtering settings per storefront and per category. Configure category and web page URL structure per storefront. Use Price Lists for custom pricing on each storefront. View and manage orders and customers for multiple storefronts in one place. Control product purchasability per storefront. Create Automatic and Coupon Promotions per storefront (using the Standard Promotions editor). Manage customer groups (like retail or wholesale) for each storefront and set the default group. Create category-level discounts per storefront for specific customer groups. Create customers and manage login access to each storefront. Control storefront status for all storefronts from Channel Manager. Filter ecommerce sales reports by native storefront channel. Collect and export newsletter subscriptions per storefront. Create and manage 301 redirects per storefront. Manage shipping methods and out of delivery zone messaging per storefront.

The same form fields are used for both the billing and shipping address, though the data your customers provide for each can be different from one another.

identifier: Address Fields: built-in required address fields
statement: There are seven built-in required address fields: First Name Last Name Address Line 1 Suburb/City Country State/Province Zip/Postcode
There are three additional built-in fields, but they are not required by default: Phone Number* Company Name Address Line 2
These fields cannot be removed, but can be renamed. The new names will be reflected on the account registration page and the customer Address Book, but not checkout.

Only the “Required” setting for Phone Number, Company Name, and Address Line 2 built-in fields can be adjusted for the Account Settings, registration, and checkout pages. All other built-in fields are required for shipping and checkout functionality and cannot be made optional.

identifier: Simple shipping address entry: country drop-down
statement: The default country in the drop-down menu is based on the customer’s IP address. Additionally, the menu only includes countries which have been set up in the Shipping page if configured.

When enabled, the built-in Phone Number field has different restrictions while and also performing number validation: Only the + special character is allowed and only as the first character for entering a country code. Only numbers are accepted. The amount of entered numbers must be valid for the country on the address. Spaces and dashes are ignored.

Enabling Google Address Autocomplete allows customers in select countries to check out faster by providing a list of potential matching addresses as the customer enters their billing or shipping address.

The country field is featured at the top of address sections as it provides context to the other fields. The remainder of fields are displayed in the order they are configured in your store’s settings.

By default, the order confirmation page displays the storewide order confirmation contact email address, or if that field is empty, the store administrator email address in your store's Miscellaneous settings.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

statement: The Contact Email field in your checkout settings allows you to specify an email address to appear on the order confirmation ("Thanks for your order") page. If you leave the Contact Email field blank, the order confirmation page displays the store administrator email address entered in your store's Miscellaneous settings.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

identifier: Checkout Settings: Contact email (the order confirmation page's phone number)
statement: Want to change the phone number on the order confirmation page? This page uses the phone number listed in the store profile.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

identifier: Customer Order Notifications: Reply-to Email Address
statement: The order confirmation email is sent from your store using the email address entered in your store profile contact information. If a customer replies to an order email message, this is the address it will attempt to deliver to.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

identifier: Customer Order Notifications: Reply-to Email Address (Using Multi-Storefront?)
statement: Using Multi-Storefront? You can use the global setting or specify a store email address per storefront. See Single-Storefront vs. Multi-Storefront for other settings moved into Channel Manager.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

identifier: International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront: Settings and launch
statement: Settings and launch — Configure key storefront settings, such as contact information, search settings, and customer privacy, and make the storefront available to shoppers.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: contact information shown to buyers), found for S02-VP-79.

identifier: Using Multiple Currencies: currency converter (a visitor's IP address)
statement: If you have multiple currencies enabled, a currency converter will display on your store that will allow customers to choose among the currencies you have set up. If a visitor's IP address matches a supported country, they will see the appropriate currency automatically.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

statement: To localize shopping experiences, you can have multiple storefronts that target specific shopper segments, regions, or brands. You can add a selector to a theme so shoppers can select the storefront they want to browse from a list of options.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

identifier: Storefront selector for multi-storefront: what you can do with the selectors
statement: You can do the following with the storefront selectors that you create and inject into a theme: * Customize the style of the switcher and its options. * Choose which pages you want the selector to appear. * Select the storefronts that you include in the selector.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74. The list's three items, in full.

identifier: Storefront selector for multi-storefront: Steps to add storefront selector data (config.json, theme_settings)
statement: Currently, there is no Stencil object for the storefront selector. Instead, you can add data for the storefront selector in the `config.json` file, which allows the selector to appear in the `theme_settings` Stencil object.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

identifier: Catalyst Multi-Storefront Setup: Configure channels in your Catalyst app (language selector)
statement: In your Catalyst app, configure which channel each locale pulls data from. When a shopper switches to a locale in the language selector, that channel's data is shown.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

statement: When a shopper creates a customer account, that account can only access the storefront on which it was created. The same login information will not work on your other native storefronts. This is the default behavior for Multi-Storefront (MSF) customer accounts, but it can be modified to allow customers to access all storefronts connected to your store. See Allowing Global Logins for more information.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

identifier: Customers and Multi-Storefront: Allowing Global Logins (origin channel)
statement: A customer’s access to storefronts outside of their origin channel is based on the Allow global logins setting for that channel. All channels can manage their settings separately in the control panel.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

identifier: Customers and Multi-Storefront: Allowing Global Logins (allow_global_login)
statement: When allow_global_login is set to true (default behavior) or Allow global logins is checked, customers created on any additional native and headless storefronts can access that channel. Note that headless storefront customers need access to the default storefront for checkout functionality.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: market selection), found for S02-VP-73 and S02-VP-74.

statement: Return settings are located under Settings › Returns in the control panel.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Yes, enable returns requests
statement: The returns system can be enabled by checking Yes, enable returns requests. Once activated, customers will be able to submit a return request from their account.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Instructions
statement: The Return Instructions field can be used to provide direction after the request has been submitted. Use this to outline what customers can expect from you, or what the procedure is for a return or exchange.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Reasons
statement: The Return Reasons field is where you provide your customers a list of acceptable reasons for returns.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: Return Actions
statement: The Return Actions field is where you can list the available resolution actions that a customer chooses from when submitting a return request.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Return Settings: reset Return Reasons and Return Actions to their default values
statement: Check the box to reset the Return Reasons and Return Actions to their default values. This setting, once saved, will also automatically translate the default values to your store’s language.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Requirements: Manage Settings and Manage Returns permissions
statement: To access Return Settings, the Manage Settings permission must be enabled on your user account. To process returns, the Manage Returns permission must be enabled on your user account.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: Creating a Returns Policy Page (Storefront › Web Pages)
statement: To create the page, go to Storefront › Web Pages. Follow the steps in Adding Web Pages and set the Page Name to “Shipping and Returns Policy” or something similar.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Processing Returns: FAQ: storefront returns in B2B Edition stores using the Buyer Portal experience
statement: Note that storefront returns are currently not supported in B2B Edition stores using the Buyer Portal experience.
scope: B2B Edition stores using the Buyer Portal experience
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Getting Started with Localization on Multi-Storefronts: Return reasons and actions
statement: You can click to enable returns for your store. The default values for return reasons and actions will be automatically translated per storefront, based on the selected default language for the storefront. See Processing Returns for more information on using this feature.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: Getting Started with Localization on Multi-Storefronts: Return reasons and actions (Watch out!)
statement: Watch out! Do not customize your store’s return reasons and actions, as this breaks the translation automation.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

identifier: International Enhancements for Multi-Storefront: FAQ: Can return reasons and actions be localized per storefront?
statement: Yes, the default values for return reasons and actions will be automatically translated per storefront, based on the default language selected per given storefront If you have customized your reasons and actions, they will not be automatically translated. See Processing Returns for more information.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: returns and cancellations), found for S02-VP-65 and S02-VP-66.

statement: Team permissions is BigCommerce's group-based access control system. It replaces per-user permission checkboxes with reusable **user groups**, predefined **policy** bundles, and per-store **targets**. A user's effective access is the union of every policy granted by every group they belong to.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **User groups** — Named, reusable bundles of access. For example, *Warehouse*, *Sales Rep*, *Finance*.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72. The list's item 1 of 3.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **Policies** — Predefined permission bundles such as *Orders Read* or *Account Users Manage*. Policies are granted to groups, not to individual users.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72. The list's item 2 of 3.

identifier: Team permissions: How team permissions works (the three concepts)
statement: **Targets** — The resource a policy applies to: a specific store, or the account itself.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72. The list's item 3 of 3.

statement: A default **Account Administrators** group is provisioned with each account and grants account-level access. Store owners and other account admins must remain members of this group to keep account-level permissions after team permissions is enabled.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

statement: A single store can have multiple users that log in to assist with the day-to-day functions of managing a store or performing a specific role in the business. Each user should have their own account, with permissions limited to only their areas of responsibility.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: Editing user permissions (Settings › Users)
statement: To edit user permissions, go to Settings › Users while logged in as the store owner or a user account with the Manage Users and Edit Users permissions enabled. Click the Action button for the desired user account, then select Edit.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Create Channels
statement: Create Channels Add channels in the Channel Manager.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

identifier: User Roles and Permissions: High-Risk Permissions: Delete Channels
statement: Delete Channels Delete channels from the Channel Manager.
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: staff access), found for S02-VP-71 and S02-VP-72.

statement: Enable transactions within AI-powered shopping experiences while remaining merchant of record.
scope: Agentic checkout
note: A2 part BC-2 (group: who sells to the buyer), found for S02-VP-63 and S02-VP-64.

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Install applications permission
statement: To install or update apps and leave reviews, you must be the store owner or have the Install applications permission enabled on your user account.
scope: a store; the store owner or a user with the Install applications permission
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). Who installs or updates a store's apps.

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Uninstall applications permission
statement: To uninstall apps or cancel an app installation, you must have the Uninstall applications permission enabled.
scope: a store; a user with the Uninstall applications permission
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). Who uninstalls a store's apps.

identifier: Using the App Marketplace: Launch applications permission
statement: To launch apps, you must be the store owner, have the Launch applications permission, or have been granted access to a multi-user Single Click App.
scope: a store; the store owner, a user with the Launch applications permission, or a user granted a multi-user Single Click App
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). Who launches a store's installed apps.

statement: View a searchable list of your installed apps by going to Apps › My apps in the control panel. From the list, you can access app details, apply updates, and uninstall apps.
scope: a store's control panel
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). Where the installed apps are listed and managed.

statement: Install applications Install apps from the App Marketplace.
scope: a user account of a store
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). The permission row, among the system admin permissions.

statement: Uninstall applications Uninstall apps from the store.
scope: a user account of a store
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). The permission row, among the system admin permissions.

identifier: Single Click Apps: third-party sales channels
statement: Note that many third-party sales channels are apps, which can only be installed by the store owner or users with the Install applications permission.
scope: a store; the store owner or a user with the Install applications permission
note: Found for S02-VP-92, who sets apps (phase A2, part A2-SA-H). Sales channels that are apps are installed by the same users.
